--adopt.Name: --adopt
--adopt.description: This behaviour is specifically intended to alter the contents of your stow directory.  If you do not want that, this option is not for you

--defer.Name: --defer
--defer.description: Don't stow files beginning with this Perl regex if the file is already stowed to another package

--delete.Name: --delete
--delete.description: Unstow the packages that follow this option from the target directory rather than installing them

--dir.Name: --dir
--dir.description: Set the stow directory to 'DIR' instead of the current directory. This also has the effect of making the default target directory be the parent of 'DIR'

--dotfiles.Name: --dotfiles
--dotfiles.description: Enable special handling for 'dotfiles' (files or folders whose name begins with a period) in the package directory. If this option is enabled, Stow will add a preprocessing step for each file or folder whose name begins with 'dot - ', and replace the 'dot- ' prefix in the name by a period (.). This is useful when Stow is used to manage collections of dotfiles, to avoid having a package directory full of hidden files

--help.Name: --help
--help.description: Show Stow command syntax, and exit

--ignore.Name: --ignore
--ignore.description: Ignore files ending in this Perl regex

--no.Name: --no
--no.description: Do not perform any operations that modify the filesystem; merely show what would happen

--no-folding.Name: --no-folding
--no-folding.description: Disable folding of newly stowed directories when stowing, and refolding of newly foldable directories when unstowing

--override.Name: --override
--override.description: Force stowing files beginning with this Perl regex if the file is already stowed to another package

--restow.Name: --restow
--restow.description: Restow packages (first unstow, then stow again). This is useful for pruning obsolete symlinks from the target tree after updating the software in a package

--stow.Name: --stow
--stow.description: Stow the packages that follow this option into the target directory. This is the default action and so can be omitted if you are only stowing packages rather than performing a mixture of stow/delete/restow actions

--target.Name: --target
--target.description: Set the target directory to 'DIR' instead of the parent of the stow directory

--verbose.Name: --verbose
--verbose.description: Send verbose output to standard error describing what Stow is doing. Verbosity levels are from 0 to 5; 0 is the default. Using '-v' or '--verbose' increases the verbosity by one; using `--verbose=N' sets it to N

-D.Name: -D
-D.description: Unstow the packages that follow this option from the target directory rather than installing them

-R.Name: -R
-R.description: Restow packages (first unstow, then stow again). This is useful for pruning obsolete symlinks from the target tree after updating the software in a package

-S.Name: -S
-S.description: Stow the packages that follow this option into the target directory. This is the default action and so can be omitted if you are only stowing packages rather than performing a mixture of stow/delete/restow actions

-d.Name: -d
-d.description: Set the stow directory to 'DIR' instead of the current directory. This also has the effect of making the default target directory be the parent of 'DIR'

-h.Name: -h
-h.description: Show Stow command syntax, and exit

-n.Name: -n
-n.description: Do not perform any operations that modify the filesystem; merely show what would happen

-t.Name: -t
-t.description: Set the target directory to 'DIR' instead of the parent of the stow directory

-v.Name: -v
-v.description: Send verbose output to standard error describing what Stow is doing. Verbosity levels are from 0 to 5; 0 is the default. Using '-v' or '--verbose' increases the verbosity by one; using `--verbose=N' sets it to N
